Subject: SIG follow-up — network topology and allowlist evidence needed

Laura / team,

Thanks again for sending the SIG starter bundle. Acme's security team is doing a targeted review of network controls before we can move to procurement. There are two items we need clarified for the SIG network section:

1) We need explicit egress IP ranges that our firewall team can allowlist for API calls from Redwood's hosted endpoints. Please provide the current stable set and an expected rotation cadence (if any).

2) Confirmation that PrivateLink (AWS Private Endpoints) is an available option for account-level isolation, plus any DNS/hostnames we should expect. If PrivateLink is not possible for our plan, we need a VPC peering diagram and the required routes/ports.

Can you also attach any packet-capture or ephemeral NAT evidence you use for audits (screenshots / short logs are fine). The security team is working to a Friday internal deadline — could we get a first response by Tuesday?

Appreciate it,
Simone
Simone Gray

security@acmehealth.org

Subject: Re: SIG follow-up — network topology and allowlist evidence needed

Hi Simone — thanks for the clear ask. We're putting together a short evidence pack and answers to the SIG network questions. High level answers below, full details and attachments are in the zip I just shared (sig-evidence-pack-2027-04-11.zip).

Quick summary:
- Egress IPs: we operate a stable set of outbound NAT ranges for hosted API traffic. Current published ranges (subject to announcements at least 30 days before rotation): 198.51.100.0/24, 198.51.101.0/24. We maintain a second cold pool (203.0.113.0/24) for failover; we will notify customers via the Console and email 30 days before any permanent change.
- Private connectivity: For enterprise plans we support AWS PrivateLink endpoints at the account level. PrivateLink hostnames are registered per-account and look like <account-id>.api.private.redwoodinference.com — TLS terminated with certs we control. If you prefer VPC peering, we can provide a peering diagram and required route table entries.
- Ports/protocols: outbound HTTPS (443) only for API calls. For VPC peering, allow TCP 443 and TCP 22 only for optional host management (disabled by default). No additional inbound ports required on customer side unless you opt into peering management.
- Evidence: included are a network topology PDF, an exported NAT translation sample (egress_ip_ranges.txt), and screenshots of PrivateLink endpoint mappings.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm whether Acme will allowlist the two primary ranges or prefers PrivateLink.
2) If PrivateLink, we'll open a ticket to provision and supply DNS hostnames and instructions (expect ~2–3 business days).
3) If peering, Hiro will send the detailed peering checklist and a sample CloudFormation template for route setup.

Looping in Hiro and Rishi for technical details and to attach the packet-decaps we captured for audit.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Director, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: SIG follow-up — network topology and allowlist evidence needed

Hey Simone — adding the technical detail requested (exported snippets below). All internal IPs and hostnames referenced are in the attached text/pdf.

1) Egress IP ranges (current):
- primary: 198.51.100.0/24
- secondary: 198.51.101.0/24
- coldfailover: 203.0.113.0/24
Rotation policy: we rotate a subset of ephemeral NAT IPs within the primary pools weekly for load distribution; permanent renumbering is rare and will have 30-day notice. For firewall allowlists, please allow the entire /24 blocks above rather than single IPs.

2) PrivateLink details:
- We publish account-scoped PrivateLink service names: com.amazonaws.vpce.amazonaws.com/redewood-<region>-<account-id> (endpoint service backs TLS with SANs for account hostnames).
- DNS: account-level CNAMEs look like <acct>.api.private.redwoodinference.com -> vpce-1234-abcdef.region.vpce.amazonaws.com
- Certificates: we terminate TLS at the PrivateLink endpoint; we rotate certs no more frequently than quarterly.

3) VPC peering (optional) checklist:
- Routes: Customer route to 10.26.0.0/16 -> peering connection; Redwood route to customer CIDR required.
- Ports: TCP 443 (API), ephemeral ephemeral (1024–65535) are NOT required — we do not initiate ephemeral flows to customers. Management access (if requested) uses bastion on TCP 22 and must be enabled explicitly.

4) Audit artifacts (attached): NAT translation sample (egress_ip_ranges.txt), PrivateLink endpoint mapping screenshot (pe_endpoint_map.png), packet capture excerpt (pcap-snippet.txt) — redacted for PHI.

If you need signed attestations for the SIG pack (date-stamped), we can include a one-page signed PDF from our network team — let me know and Rishi will provide.

-Hiro
Hiro Tanaka
Senior Infrastructure Engineer — Redwood Inference
hiro.tanaka@redwoodinference.com
